course.name: HTML5 Fundamentals
course.description: A comprehensive 3-day course covering HTML5 fundamentals, structured content, forms, tables, semantic elements, multimedia integration, canvas drawing, and web accessibility. Students will build progressively more complex web pages and forms, learning best practices for modern HTML5 development.

lessons.title: Day 1 — HTML Structure & Tags
lessons.content: # Day 1 — HTML Structure & Tags ## Learning Objectives By the end of this day, you will be able to: - Create a complete, valid HTML5 document structure - Use heading tags (h1-h6) appropriately for document hierarchy - Apply paragraph, link, and image tags correctly - Structure content using lists and divisions - Understand the role of the DOCTYPE declaration ## HTML5 Document Structure HTML5 introduced a simplified document structure with the declaration. Every HTML5 document follows this basic structure: ```html Page Title ``` ## Essential Tags - **** — Declares HTML5 document type (must be lowercase!) - **** — Root element of the page (use lang attribute for accessibility) - **** — Contains metadata, title, and link elements - **** — Sets character encoding to support all Unicode characters - **** — Makes page responsive on mobile devices - **** — Page title shown in browser tab and bookmarks - **<body>** — Main content area visible to users ## Heading Tags (h1-h6) Headings create a hierarchy for your content: - **<h1>** — Primary page heading (only one per page) - **<h2>** — Section heading - **<h3>** — Subsection heading - **<h4>, <h5>, <h6>** — Deeper nesting levels ## Paragraph and Text Tags - **<p>** — Paragraph element for text blocks - **<br>** — Line break (use sparingly) - **<hr>** — Thematic break or section divider - **<strong>** — Important text (semantically bold) - **<em>** — Emphasized text (semantically italic) ## Link Tags - **<a href="url">** — Hyperlink (href is required) - **href="#"** — Placeholder link - **href="mailto:email@example.com"** — Email link - **target="_blank"** — Opens link in new tab ## Image Tags - **<img src="image.jpg" alt="description">** — Image element - **alt** attribute is required for accessibility - **width** and **height** attributes improve page load performance ## List Tags - **<ul>** — Unordered (bulleted) list - **<ol>** — Ordered (numbered) list - **<li>** — List item - **<dl>** — Definition list with **<dt>** (term) and **<dd>** (description) ## Division and Span - **<div>** — Block-level container for grouping - **<span>** — Inline container for text styling - Use semantic class names for easier styling

content_payload.title: Practical Task: HTML Page Structure
content_payload.description: Create a complete personal profile page that demonstrates proper HTML5 document structure and semantic tag usage.
requirements: Create an HTML file named profile.html with valid HTML5 doctype
Include proper meta charset and viewport tags in the head
Add a unique <title> tag with your name
Create a main heading using <h1> with your name
Include at least one <h2> and one <h3> following the heading hierarchy

Add a paragraph about yourself using

tags
Create an unordered list of 3-5 hobbies using <ul> and <li>
Add an image of yourself with descriptive alt text
Include at least 2 external links using <a> tags with proper href attributes
Group related sections using <div> or semantic HTML5 elements

content_payload.title: Assignment: Multi-Section HTML Page
content_payload.description: Build a comprehensive multi-section webpage that showcases all the HTML structure and tag concepts learned today. This should be a well-organized document with multiple content sections.
requirements: Create a complete HTML5 document with proper structure
Include at least 4 distinct content sections (each with its own <h2>)
Use all 6 heading levels (h1-h6) appropriately across sections
Include both ordered and unordered lists in different sections
Add definition list using <dl>, <dt>, and <dd> in at least one section
Include an image with responsive width using max-width: 100% styling
Create a navigation section with internal anchor links to other sections
Use <div> containers to group related content elements
Validate the HTML using an online validator to ensure no errors
Submit the code to GitHub with a descriptive README.md
